title: 1978 AHSME Problem 29
statement: Sides \(AB,\) \(BC,\) \(CD,\) and \(DA,\) respectively, of convex quadrilateral \(ABCD\) are extended past \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) and \(A\) to points \(B',\) \(C',\) \(D',\) and \(A'.\) Also, \(AB=BB'=6,\) \(BC=CC'=7,\) \(CD=DD'=8,\) and \(DA=AA'=9;\) and the area of \(ABCD\) is \(10.\) The area of \(A'B'C'D'\) is

solutions.text:
Using position vectors, the equal extensions give \[ \begin{aligned} A'&=2A-D,& B'&=2B-A,\\ C'&=2C-B,& D'&=2D-C. \end{aligned} \] Substitution into the oriented polygon-area sum shows that the diagonal cross terms cancel: \[ \begin{aligned} &A'\mathbin{\times}B' +B'\mathbin{\times}C'\\ &\quad+C'\mathbin{\times}D' +D'\mathbin{\times}A'\\ &=5A\mathbin{\times}B +5B\mathbin{\times}C\\ &\quad+5C\mathbin{\times}D +5D\mathbin{\times}A. \end{aligned} \] Hence the outer area is five times the original area, or \(5\cdot10=50.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
